blocks.text: **Why it matters:** Mexican cooking rests on chillies, corn and beans. A dried chilli is a different ingredient from its fresh form, and corn treated with lime is a different food from plain ground corn. Both have to be understood before the salsas and tortillas make sense.

**You need:** three dried chillies (*ancho*, *guajillo*, *chipotle*); a fresh chilli (jalapeño or serrano); a dry heavy pan; hot water; a blender; onion, garlic, salt, lime; tongs; gloves for handling chillies; the lens template; tasting forms.
**Explanation:**
*Chillies, fresh and dried:*

items.text: **fresh** (jalapeño, serrano, *poblano*): brightness and heat;
**dried** (*ancho*, *guajillo*, *pasilla*, *chipotle*): toasted, soaked and blended for depth, colour and sweetness.

blocks.text: A dried chilli is a different ingredient from its fresh form: an *ancho* is a dried *poblano*, and tastes of raisins and cocoa rather than green pepper.
*Toasting dried chillies.* Seeds and stems out; flat on a dry, hot pan for seconds per side, until fragrant and just pliable; then soaked in hot water. A few seconds too long and they turn bitter.

*Corn and* nixtamal. Dried corn is cooked with lime (calcium hydroxide, *cal*). This loosens the hulls, makes the dough hold together and improves its nutrition. The treated corn is ground into *masa* for tortillas and *tamales*.

*Beans.* Black or pinto beans cooked slowly with onion and herbs (*epazote*), often refried. Dried beans follow the bean rule of §9: soaked for at least 5 hours with the water poured away, then boiled in fresh water for at least 30 minutes.
*Regional styles:*

items.text: **the north:** wheat tortillas, grilled beef;
**Oaxaca:** moles, cheese;
**the Yucatán:** achiote, sour orange, pit-cooking;
**central Mexico:** street food, *tacos*.

blocks.text: *Meal structure and drinks.* The main meal at midday; tortillas at every meal; salsas on the table. *Agua fresca* (fruit or flower water), water, beer.
**Practice:**

items.text: **A chilli tasting (60 min).** Three dried chillies toasted, soaked and blended into small salsas, with salt and a little garlic; a fresh salsa alongside. Taste each for heat, sweetness and smoke.

blocks.text: **Look for:** you can tell *ancho*, *guajillo* and *chipotle* apart by taste and use.
**If it goes wrong:**

rows: Seconds per side; off when fragrant
Whole dried chillies, chosen by taste
Seeds out before toasting; blend longer or sieve

blocks.text: **Safety:** gloves for cutting chillies, and hands kept from the eyes; the extraction on while toasting (the fumes sting).
**Record:** the tasting form for each chilli, and the lens notes.
**Why it matters:** salsas give a Mexican meal its brightness; a braise in a dried-chilli sauce gives it depth. The same chillies do both jobs, prepared two different ways.

**You need:** Dutch tomatoes (in summer), onion, a fresh chilli, coriander, lime; tomatillos, or green tomatoes from a late-season glut; dried chillies; garlic and spices (cumin, oregano); pork shoulder or chicken legs; a dry heavy pan; a blender; a heavy casserole; the probe.
**Explanation:**
*Fresh salsas:*

items.text: ***pico de gallo*:** tomato, onion, chilli, coriander and lime, in summer with Dutch tomatoes;
**a raw green salsa;**
seasoned and balanced, kept in the fridge, and out for at most 2 hours (§9).

blocks.text: *Cooked salsas.* Tomatoes or tomatillos (green tomatoes stand in), chillies, onion and garlic charred on a dry pan (`VEG-3.M2`), then blended. A toasted-dried-chilli salsa is made the same way, from soaked chillies.
*A braise in a chilli sauce:*

items.text: Toast, soak and drain the dried chillies.
Blend them with aromatics, spices and some of the soaking liquid into a smooth sauce.
Fry the sauce briefly in hot fat, stirring, until it darkens and thickens. This deepens it; skipping it leaves a raw taste.
Braise pork shoulder or chicken legs in it until tender (`SLW-3`). Chicken is cooked to 75 °C.

blocks.text: *Balance.* Heat against acid, salt and a little sweetness. Choose the salsa to contrast the braise: a sharp, fresh salsa against a deep, rich sauce.
**Practice:**

items.text: **Two salsas (60 min).** A fresh salsa and a charred, blended salsa.
**The braise (90 min active, 3 h in total).** A pork or chicken braise in a dried-chilli sauce.

blocks.text: **Look for:** salsas bright and balanced; a deep red, glossy braising sauce; tender meat.
**If it goes wrong:**

rows: Seconds per side; discard any that blacken
Fry it in hot fat until it darkens
Lime and salt, tasted in steps
In the fridge; out for at most 2 hours

blocks.text: **Safety:** the blended sauce spits when it hits the hot fat: a deep pan, a lid at hand, the arm clear; chicken to 75 °C (§9); salsas out for at most 2 hours.
**Record:** the chillies, the sauce steps, the braise time, and the balance notes.
**Why it matters:** a corn tortilla is made from corn alone, because the corn has been treated with lime. A good one puffs on the pan and stays pliable; a dry dough or a cool pan gives a stiff disc.

**You need:** *masa harina*; warm water; salt; a tortilla press, or a heavy pan and two sheets of plastic (a freezer bag cut open); a dry cast-iron pan or *comal*; a cloth; fillings, onion, coriander and a salsa for tacos; for the *tamales*, lard or another fat, stock, corn husks soaked in hot water, a steamer.
**Explanation:**
*Nixtamalización.* The lime treatment of corn (`CUI-3.M9.L1`) is why tortillas can be made from corn alone. *Masa harina* is dried, ground *nixtamal* corn, mixed with water to a dough.
*Corn tortillas:*

items.text: Mix *masa harina* and warm water to a soft, smooth dough, like play-dough, and rest it.
Press a small ball: if the edges crack, the dough is too dry. Add water a little at a time until they don't.
Press the balls between two sheets of plastic in a tortilla press, or with a heavy pan.
Cook on a dry, hot cast-iron pan: turn once, then again. A good tortilla puffs.
Keep them warm, stacked and wrapped in a cloth, where they steam and stay pliable.

blocks.text: *Tacos.* A warm tortilla, a filling, a salsa, onion and coriander. Keep them simple.
*A simple* tamal:

items.text: Beat *masa* with fat and stock until light.
Spread it on a soaked corn husk, add a filling, and fold.
Steam until the *masa* comes away from the husk.

blocks.text: **Practice:**

items.text: **Tortillas (75 min).** A batch pressed and cooked; the puff photographed; tacos.
***Tamales* (75 min active, 2 h in total).** A small batch with a vegetable or the braise as the filling, steamed.

blocks.text: **Look for:** tortillas that puff and stay pliable; *tamales* that come away from the husk.
**If it goes wrong:**

rows: Water a little at a time; rest again
Heat the pan well; turn once, then again
Wrap in a cloth as they come off

blocks.text: **Safety:** a braise used as a filling reheated until steaming hot throughout and not reheated again; the steamer lid lifted away from you; the hot pan's handle covered.
**Record:** the water added to the dough, the photo of the puff, and the *tamal* steaming time.
**Why it matters:** at a Mexican table, the heat is set by each eater, not by the cook. Planning heat levels lets children and guests who don't like heat eat the same meal.
**You need:** tortillas (or the dough); two salsas; a braise or a grilled centre (`FIR-3`); beans; a fresh side; an *agua fresca*; labels for the salsas; the timeline; the household or guest cards.
**Explanation:**
*The meal:*

items.text: warm tortillas;
two salsas, one fresh and one cooked;
a braise or a grilled centre;
beans;
a fresh side: a cabbage and radish slaw, sliced radishes, or pickled onions;
an *agua fresca*, for example with Dutch rhubarb (the stalks only), cucumber and lime, or dried hibiscus flowers.

blocks.text: *Heat levels for the table:*

items.text: the main dishes moderately hot;
the heat added at the table, through salsas of different strengths, each labelled;
a mild option for children and for guests who don't like heat.

blocks.text: *Timing:*

items.text: the braise ahead: it holds and improves, and is reheated until steaming hot throughout;
the salsas and slaw ahead, kept cold;
the tortillas cooked last and kept warm in a cloth, or cooked in batches through the meal.

blocks.text: *A fresh, sharp side.* A rich braise and beans need something sharp and crunchy beside them: pickled onions, radishes, or a lime-dressed slaw.
*Labelling the salsas.* Write each salsa's heat on a card beside it (mild, medium, hot), and taste them in that order yourself before the meal, so the labels match.
**Practice:**

items.text: **The meal (3 h).** A Mexican meal for the household or guests, the heat levels planned.

blocks.text: **Look for:** everyone can eat at their own heat; warm tortillas throughout.
**If it goes wrong:**

rows: Moderate dishes; heat in the salsas
Cook last; wrap in a cloth; batches

blocks.text: **Safety:** salsas and slaw out for at most 2 hours (§9); the braise reheated until steaming hot throughout; the heat levels labelled for guests.
**Record:** the heat plan, the labels, the timeline, and the cards.

blocks.text: **Task:** cook a Mexican meal with layered flavour, and heat set by the table.

items.text: **The brief:** tortillas, two salsas, a braise or grilled centre, beans, a fresh side and a drink.
**The constraints:** a flavour plan for the braise and the salsas; heat levels planned and labelled; Dutch seasonal produce, with every substitution named.
**The criteria:** household cards on balance and recognition.
**The record:** the flavour plans, the heat plan, the substitutions, photos and the cards.

blocks.text: **You need:** dried and fresh chillies, *masa harina*, the braise's cut, beans, seasonal vegetables, coriander, limes; the probe; the household cards.
*Procedure:*

items.text: Plan the meal, the flavour plans and the heat levels; write the substitutions with their effect.
Cook the braise and the beans ahead; make the salsas and the fresh side, and keep them cold; the tortillas last.
Serve, with the salsas labelled; collect the cards; note which heat level each taster chose.

blocks.text: **Show:**

items.text: **`CK-CUIS` level 3, the Mexican part:** with `CUI-3.M9.X2`, two dishes recognised by their style and the tasters.

blocks.text: AI review reads the plans and the cards: *competent* is every part of the brief, a braise and salsas with written flavour plans, labelled heat levels and the substitutions named; *not yet* is one heat level for everything, or no flavour plan.

blocks.text: **Task:** make corn tortillas from *masa harina* that puff, and serve them as tacos. Press and cook a batch on a dry pan, adjusting the dough by feel (note the adjustment), and photograph the puff. Serve them as tacos with a filling and two salsas. Scale the batch for guests, or adjust the dough for a different *masa harina* (one element adapted for quantity or conditions).
**You need:** *masa harina*, water, a filling, the salsas' ingredients; a tortilla press or a heavy pan; the dry pan; a cloth; the household cards.
**Framework:** the tortillas.

rows: *Masa harina* and warm water; soft, like play-dough; rested
Water added until the edges don't crack
A dry, hot pan; turned once, then again; puffs
A filling, two salsas, onion, coriander
Scaled for guests, or another *masa harina*

items.text: Mix, rest and adjust the dough; note the adjustment.
Press and cook; photograph the puff.
